title: The gift came with conditions
text: Grant Larceny has died at the gala after his private toast. His proposed gift agreement is still unsigned. These are the terms he intended to announce tonight.
rows: Artie Ficial must resign within sixty days

title: An empty bottle in preparation
text: I found the newly acquired poison bottle empty after the preparation-room tour. Its paper seal was broken. I locked the room and retained the bottle for examination. It had been brought out for the condition inspection of Grant’s proposed exhibition centerpiece. Signed: Collections Assistant.
rows: The Velvet Widow poison bottle / acquisition lot 73

title: What happened to Grant’s glass
text: These are my setup photos. I stayed with the wrapped glass until 6:40. From 6:40 to 6:44, I was away from the table. After sealing the cover at 6:44, I watched it until I opened it to pour. I then watched Grant’s glass until his 6:49 toast. The same glass was used throughout. Signed: Service Manager.

title: When the bottle was accessible
text: The bottle was kept locked away before the tour. It was put on the visitor-side shelf when the room opened and locked away again at closing. Nobody obtained it outside those eight minutes. The laboratory matched material remaining in the bottle to residue inside Grant’s glass.
rows: Bottle full; original paper seal intact
No other bottles brought out or given to guests

appendix.title: Two different ways to approach preparation
rows: Papers pass through a small slot
Guests can enter and reach the shelf
appendix.text: The west return counter is outside a solid wall. Its small slot passes papers and support sleeves, not people. Staff did not pass the bottle or its contents through it. The east doorway is the only guest entrance to the shelves.

title: The glass, not the punch
text: Cyanide was found on the inside of Grant’s glass. Samples of the shared punch and food were clear. Material remaining in the acquired poison bottle matches the residue in the glass. The lab result identifies the poisoned object; the caterer’s record establishes how it was handled.

appendix.title: Two details from the museum’s records
rows: Logo sticker across a closed seam
appendix.text: The museum-logo sticker bridged the sealed plastic wrapping. The placemat’s logo was sewn into cloth. They are different objects. The receiving desk first used its raised RECEIVED stamp at 6:45. Earlier working copies had flat red-pencil corrections, not that stamp.
